transcript.text: gas hob keeps clickin on its own since i cleand it, stops then starts agen. drivin me mad. pls help

That uncommanded clicking is almost probably caused by moisture or a misaligned part left after cleaning. Gas hobs use an electrode to spark; if water or grease bridges the gap between the electrode and the burner cap, or if the cap isn't sitting flat, it tricks the system into thinking it should keep sparking even when no one has turned the knob. Please do this check:
1. Make sure the hob is switched off at the wall (isolate the power).
2. Lift off each burner cap and crown (the metal rings over the gas holes). They usually just lift up; don't force them.
3. Dry them thoroughly with a cloth, including the white ceramic ignition tip underneath where they sit.
4. Wipe the base of the hob clean of any water or cleaning residue.
5. Re-seat each cap so it sits perfectly flat and square (no wobbling). Once that's done, try lighting one burner normally. Does the clicking stop when you turn the knob, or does it still click on its own?

ok did it. unpluged the hob under the sink for the afternoon n the clicking has stopped. one cap was a bit wonky so i put it back flat, n wiped some grease off. burners light ok when i use them. no gas smell btw

That’s excellent news. It was exactly what I suspected: moisture and grease from the cleaning were bridging the ignition gap, tricking the spark module into firing continuously. Leaving it unplugged allowed everything to dry out completely. To stop this happening again after future cleanings, just make sure you leave the hob unplugged for a few hours (or overnight) after washing it so any water trapped under the caps or around the electrodes has time to evaporate fully before you plug it back in. Also, double-check that every cap sits perfectly flat and square. Since it’s working normally now with no gas smell, there’s nothing else to do. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
